ap_physics_1-m01.set_intro: A soccer ball is kicked from a level field with an initial speed of $16\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $53^\circ$ above the horizontal. The ball lands on the same level field. Air resistance is negligible.

stimulus.description: A soccer ball is kicked from a level field with an initial speed of $16\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $53^\circ$ above the horizontal. The ball lands on the same level field. Air resistance is negligible.

items.stem: What is the speed of the ball at the highest point of its flight?

options.why: Reports the full launch speed, assuming the speed does not change on the way up.
Subtracts the vertical component from the launch speed.
At the top the vertical velocity is zero and the horizontal velocity has not changed, so the speed is $v_0\cos\theta=(16)\cos 53^\circ=9.63\text{ m/s}$.
Reports the vertical component of the launch velocity instead of the horizontal one.

items.stem: How long is the ball in the air?

options.why: Gives the time to reach the highest point only, $v_y/g$, not the whole flight.

Uses the full launch speed in $2v_0/g$ as if the ball were kicked straight up.
The vertical motion returns to the launch height after $t=2v_0\sin\theta/g=2(12.8)/9.8=2.61\text{ s}$.

ap_physics_1-m02.set_intro: Two students pull on the same sled of mass $50\text{ kg}$ that rests on frictionless ice. One student pulls with a constant horizontal force of $30\text{ N}$ due east and the other pulls with a constant horizontal force of $120\text{ N}$ due north. No other horizontal force acts on the sled.

stimulus.description: Two students pull on the same sled of mass $50\text{ kg}$ that rests on frictionless ice. One student pulls with a constant horizontal force of $30\text{ N}$ due east and the other pulls with a constant horizontal force of $120\text{ N}$ due north. No other horizontal force acts on the sled.

items.stem: What is the magnitude of the net force on the sled?

options.why: Subtracts the smaller force from the larger one, as if they were opposite.
Averages the two forces.
The two forces are perpendicular, so the magnitude of the net force is $\sqrt{F_1^2+F_2^2}=\sqrt{(30)^2+(120)^2}=124\text{ N}$.
Adds the magnitudes of the two forces as if they pointed in the same direction.

blueprint.subject: ap_physics_1
blueprint.concept: Two questions about a sled pulled by two perpendicular horizontal forces
student_thinking: Add the two forces as perpendicular vectors, not as numbers
Apply Newton's second law to the net force

key_conditions.condition: the ice is frictionless and only the two pulls act horizontally
key_conditions.evidence: the shared stimulus states the ice is frictionless and no other horizontal force acts

misconceptions.description: Subtracts the smaller force from the larger one, as if they were opposite.
Averages the two forces.
Adds the magnitudes of the two forces as if they pointed in the same direction.

verification.independent_path: the perpendicular components are added as vectors with numpy and the acceleration vector is the net force divided by the mass

items.stem: What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the sled?

options.why: Divides the sum of the magnitudes by the mass.
Divides the difference of the forces by the mass.
Divides the net force by twice the mass.
The acceleration is along the net force, so $a=F_{net}/m=124/50=2.47\text{ m/s}^2$.
